key_insight: Strong internal stroke-classification performance did not generalize across centers, with F1 falling from 95.48% to approximately 58–62% on external validation.
clinical_relevance: Low ischemic-stroke sensitivity and a tendency toward hemorrhage overdiagnosis raise concerns about reliability in acute stroke triage.
method: Three-channel CT preprocessing used radiological Hounsfield Unit windows in asymmetric .mat and .png formats.
CNN and Vision Transformer features were combined through cross-attention fusion.
Training used Integrated Orthogonal-Focal Loss; evaluation included external datasets and multi-seed stability analysis.
evidence_signal: External evaluation on AISD, BHSD, and PhysioNet using a Mask Anchor filter showed reduced performance, with reported ischemic-stroke precision of 77% and sensitivity of 57%.
watch_item: DenseNet201+ViT showed the lowest multi-seed variability, but stability alone does not establish clinical readiness given the external performance gap.
paper_title: Acute Stroke Classification Using Asymmetric Data Standardization and Orthogonal-Focal Loss Optimized CNN-ViT Cross-Attention Fusion: A Multicenter External Validation Study
